content.comment_body: Hello, I have a rotary flow sensor and a hall effect sensor, both providing frequency pulse inputs. By adjusting an actuator valve with a 0-10V output, my goal is to regulate the flow so that the flow meter frequency is twice that of the hall effect sensor. The hall effect sensor mounts to a generator axle, which is connected to a load box. As the load is manually adjusted, the resulting increase in torque requires the actuator valve to open further to ensure adequate flow. Ideally, I want the system to rely only on load manipulation, with no other external controls involved. Any suggestions are appreciated. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user seeks automation for controlling a flow actuator valve using sensor frequencies, aiming for a specific ratio between two sensors. They want the valve to respond to variations in load without introducing extra control methods. This setup requires reliable in-system logic and streamlined integration of hardware and automated controls to continuously maintain the desired operational relationship under changing conditions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the flow control to self-adjust through the actuator automatically, based on load changes alone, with no supplementary controls, focusing on a seamless and autonomous operation.
